HUE Animation Studio: Complete Stop Motion Animation Kit (Camera, Software, Book) for Windows/macOS (Black) Our ten year old grandson has been using a Lego stop action kit for about two years. From what I understood he was becoming unhappy with the quality and positioning capabilities of the camera he was using. The software may have also been a bit clumsy. We decided on the Hue Animation Studio kit (with camera) after surveying many stop-action offerings. Some were quite advanced with features far beyond making stop-action videos, while others appeared to be targeted at a younger child. Few, if any, included a high quality camera. We noticed that the Hue Animation camera alone received excellent reviews. We decided try the whole kit for only $20 more than the camera alone.

Our grandson absolutely loves this kit. The images from the camera a great and it is easy to put into many stable positions. He also likes the software much better than what he had been using before. The build quality of the camera appears to be very good and it should be durable. I think we hit a home run for this ten year old.

Tech2 Three Sided Surge Protector Cube with 3 Outlets & USB Ports (Smart 3A Total) ETL Certified Adapter for Home, School, or Office This surge protector cube from Tech2 is great! It’s compact but has 3 AC outlets and 3 USB ports. The latter is especially useful since so many devices don’t include wall adapters anymore.

The output for the USB ports is 5V, 3A Max.

The USB ports glow blue whether you use them or not. The blue light is bright during the day and night, and can be seen even when there is a cable plugged into a port. I like and don’t like the illumination. It’s helpful at night if I need to plug something in, but then, the light is very bright in a dark room.

The cube doesn’t block the outlet below it, which I also like. If plugged into the bottom outlet on a normal wall socket, it will block the top outlet.

I like the small size, it’s great for keeping in your bag in case you need a bunch of outlets. But it’s also functional at home, and has replaced one of my bulky power strips.

The surge protector is made in China.

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Ultimate Ears 600vi Noise-Isolating Headset - Dark Silver These are amazing. They will fit. My ears are tiny. Most ear buds hurt after a while. With the smallest adapter in, these fit fine. The adapters cover a wide range of sizes, so you do need to test them all and find the best size for your ears. They work in two "modes" and I'm not sure they're supposed to. If you just sort of seat them in your ears, they act like normal earbuds (good for when you need some awareness of your surroundings). If you insert them the way you would ear plugs they act like noise cancelling earbuds (good for when you don't want to listen to the lady on the bus explain the ins and outs of her new baby's diaper). It just depends on how you sit them in your ears.

The sound quality excellent. I needed to turn down most of my devices because these transmit at a good volume--awesome if you like your music loud. The volume can be controlled on the cord. The microphone works nicely--I used mine with a Droid and the sound quality was fine. You can pause your MP3 player by pushing the button on the cord. Perfect for listening to podcasts and audiobooks.

They come with a carry case, which I thought a bit much for headphones, but I think I'll be using it. These are very good headphones, worthy of such care, and I want them to last a long time.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Ultimate Ears 600vi Noise-Isolating Headset - Dark Silver

text_fidelity_a:
Dolica GX600B200 Proline GX Series 60-Inch Aluminum Tripod and Ball Head Combo for DSLR This review is for the Dolica GX600B200 Proline GX Series 60-Inch Aluminum Tripod and Ball Head Combo for DSLR.

The pros:
-Light weight for a full-sized 60-inch tripod, especially for one made of aluminum.
-Unlike some other reviewers, I really like the carrying bag. The tripod fits just fine as long as the legs are telescoped fully, and the bag seems like it is well made. It has a zippered pocket on the inside with two spare hex keys.
-Pan function is very smooth. I don't shoot video often, but I can see that this feature will be very nice for those times when I do.
-Textured rubber feet grip well, and there are metal spikes which can be revealed if needed for extra grip on ice.
-Quick-release plate is metal instead of plastic. It also can be adjusted from side to side so that it can conform to a battery hatch on the bottom of a DSLR.

Cons:
-My biggest complaint is that there is no handle to maneuver the ball head. This makes it very difficult to make fine adjustments. A removable handle, or any sort of handle for that matter, would be a massive improvement for this tripod.
-The bubble level is on the body of the tripod. It should be on the ball head where it might actually be useful.
-The release locks on the legs are absurdly stiff to open. This makes it more difficult to extend them quickly, and also makes the tripod a very poor choice for anyone with arthritic hands. I believe it will also make it quite difficult to use in cold weather with cold, stiff fingers.
-The central column is very wobbly when fully extended, and the thumb screw used to stabilize it is totally insufficient for the task.
- Edited to add: after use in the field I found that the tripod maintains a certain amount of wobble for a few seconds after handling it, or in a breeze. It's not terribly sturdy compared to similar tripods.

Overall thoughts:
This tripod seems like a good compromise for weight and price. If I wanted a lighter tripod of higher quality I would have to spend a lot more money and get a carbon fiber tripod. I do regret the lack of a handle on the ball head. While it is not terribly sturdy, and I would not rely on this tripod extended to full height with heavy glass on the camera, for casual use it seems like it will work just fine.
text_fidelity_b: Dolica GX600B200 Proline GX Series 60-Inch Aluminum Tripod and Ball Head Combo for DSLR

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech G502 Proteus Spectrum RGB Tunable Gaming Mouse, 12,000 DPI On-The-Fly DPI Shifting, Personalized Weight and Balance Tuning with (5) 3.6g Weights, 11 Programmable Buttons I’m not a hardcore gamer anymore, so for the past few years, I’ve been using a Logitech M570 Wireless Trackball (thumb trackball). I like trackballs for everyday use, and it’s adequate for casual World of Warcraft playing. Most of the time I just futz around leveling alts or doing 5 mans with friends.

But lately I’ve been wanting a mouse I can customize, with more options to adjust my playstyle. It’s cold in my house in the winter, so I wanted to set up mouseover macros and use more mouse buttons, because my hands are cold sitting on the keyboard. So the G502 Proteus Spectrum seemed like a good mouse to review.

I just had one problem: my computer can’t customize the mouse. Why? I have a Mac Book Air.

Now, I know the G502 says on the box that it supports Windows. There’s no mention of Mac support. But I’ve never had a problem with my Mac recognizing Logitech mice, so I figured I’d be safe. What I didn’t know is that Logitech gaming mice have separate software from the Logitech Control Center for regular Logitech mice.

After some Googling, I found the Logitech Gaming Software, which supports Mac OS X 10.8.x and up. I installed it on a Mavericks machine and a Yosemite machine. Neither computer’s Logitech Gaming Software was able to find the mouse. The G502 Proteus CORE is supported, but not the G502 Proteus SPECTRUM.

So right now, I’m unable to customize any of the extra buttons or RGB lighting or any of the other special features. It’s a really fancy basic mouse. I will continue to check for Proteus Spectrum support in the Mac Logitech Gaming Center, and update this review when I can customize things. I’m going into so much detail on the Mac side of things because I know I’m not the only Mac person who tried to use this mouse. I think there’s a workaround with Bootcamp or using a Windows computer, but I’m unable to try that.

I did use the mouse for a few weeks, to test the comfort. I’m really picky on how mice feel in my hand. I’m female and have smaller hands. I like how this mouse didn’t feel too short, and it wasn’t too heavy or wide for me to use comfortably for hours at a time. I also liked the included weights, so you can adjust the weight of the mouse. I haven’t had a mouse with an adjustable weight before, and I liked that extra level of customization.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech G502 Proteus Spectrum RGB Tunable Gaming Mouse, 12,000 DPI On-The-Fly DPI Shifting, Personalized Weight and Balance Tuning with (5) 3.6g Weights, 11 Programmable Buttons

text_fidelity_a:
Acer Aspire R 15 2-in-1 Laptop, 15.6" Full HD Touch, 7th Gen Intel Core i7, GeForce 940MX, 12GB DDR4, 256GB SSD, R5-571TG-7229 This will be a fairly detailed and honest review.

1. Who is this for?
This computer is what I would consider a gateway computer. Those who are looking at upgrading a fairly old or not so powerful laptop and are looking to do a little more productivity, this is a great option.

2. What do you get?
Well you can probably read the description, however it's worth noting. You get an Intel i7 7500u CPU (dual core with 4 threads) 12gb DDR4 RAM, Nvidia 940mx GPU, a 256gb SSD, 15.6" 1080p screen, fingerprint reader, and a backlit keyboard.

The reason I mention all of the feautures is because you would be hardpressed to find another laptop with these features for the same price. To my knowledge there is not laptop on the market for $800 with an i7, dedicated graphics, 12gb of RAM and an SSD. This is really one of the best values on the market right now.

With all of that said, this isn't for everyone. If you want to do extensive gaming, this is not for you. Can it game? Yes, light gaming can be achieved, however it isn't marketed as a gaming laptop. Is this for someone who wants to do editing (video, audio, photos)? Yes, again light editing can be achieved.

What blew me away with this computer is the speakers! They are fantastic! I usually use headphones and would consider myself somewhat picky with sound, and for laptop speakers these are really something great.

This computer is really a middle of the pack all arounders dream. If you dabble in a little of this and a little of that but don't do anything professionally or extremely serious, this is really all you need.

Also, everyone's experience is different. Some hate loud fans, and if this is pushed the fans will be audible. Some don't like that the backlit keyboard times out after 30 seconds of no use. These things really don't bother me.

Lastly, the versatility of this laptop is really great. I've bought tablets and sold them because I couldn't justify having a laptop and tablet, then bought tablets again because I missed the things I could do with them that I was missing on a laptop. This solved all of those issues except size. It's pretty big, which for some is a plus others its not.

Overall, if you are looking at upgrading and don't want to spend $1,200-2,000 on a flagship model laptop this is a great option! I can't recommend this enough.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Aspire R 15 2-in-1 Laptop, 15.6" Full HD Touch, 7th Gen Intel Core i7, GeForce 940MX, 12GB DDR4, 256GB SSD, R5-571TG-7229

text_fidelity_a:
SanDisk iXpand 16GB Mobile Flash Drive with Lightning Connector for iPhones, iPads & Computers (SDIX-016G-G57) I bought this because I was traveling abroad and I wanted to backup my phone pictures. If my phone got lost or stolen on the last day of the trip, I would lose all my pictures from the entire trip. It's definitely better to backup your pictures each evening so they most you could ever lose would be the pictures from 1 day. You would still have the rest.

This is mostly just an issue when traveling abroad. Back home where WiFi is common, the iCloud backup is just fine. Unless you take zillions of pictures, you can even use your cell data to backup your pictures when there's no WiFi (assuming you have a reasonable data plan). However, when traveling abroad or on a cruise, access to the cloud can be quite expensive and/or limited. That's where this device comes in handy. Backup your pictures without WiFi or cell data.

There is another reason why you might want this device. If you take tons of pictures on your phone, then space can be a problem. You might be running out of space on your phone and/or the cloud. Or maybe you don't have an iCloud account at all. You want to make room on your phone, but you also want to keep all the pictures. You can copy your pictures to this device, and delete them off the phone to make room for more pictures.

The concept of backup up pictures from your phone is a good one, but I don't think this device is the best way to do it. I just bought the RAVPower FileHub wireless travel router, SD card reader, USB portable drive companion. I think that's going to end up being a better solution than this device.

There are a couple of things I don't like about this device:
1) The drive is very wide. If you have two USB ports that are close to each other, the drive will block the other port.
2) I find the connection to the iPhone to be awkward. The lightning connector on the device is on the end of this flexible rubber arm on the side of the device. You bend this arm away from the device (but not too far, per the warning in the instructions), and plug it into the phone. It's hard to describe, but you end up with this thing at an awkward angle hanging off the bottom of the phone. You wouldn't want to put it in your pocket like that, and it sits funny on the table since both the phone and the device are at an angle. If you flip the device around, you can get the phone to lay flat on the table, but then the device is blocking the home button. It's a really goofy design.
3) This last one takes a while to explain. There is a sync mode, where you can automatically sync the device with your phone. This will save any new pictures from your phone onto the drive. Here's how it works: You run the app, plug the device into the lightning connector, and run the sync. Pictures are copied to a folder on the drive that you specify. Since you create the folder originally, and you associate the phone's sync with that folder, you can use the device with multiple phones. Simply use a different folder for each phone. When you sync, any new pictures on the phone which aren't already in the sync folder will be copied to the drive. The concept is very good.

However, one huge drawback of the sync is that the file named aren't preserved. For example, if you just copy a picture off your phone using some other method, you'll get something like "IMG_2841". That's an easy name to deal with, if you want to do something with a particular picture (e.g. Bob wants a copy of IMG_1531, or I want to print an 8x10 of IMG_2316).

Unfortunately, when you use the sync method, the file names are not preserved. The picture files get really long names with a seemingly random string of characters. I'm sure the names mean something to the sync program, but for a human they just look like random garbage. In any case, your drive ends up with this sync folder filled with hundreds (or thousands) of files with random unreadable names. If you want to do anything with the files, you'll wish they had more recognizable names.

Let's say for example that you copied IMG_1000 and IMG_1001 off your phone using some other method, and later you decide you also want IMG_1002. Well, you know that the picture must be in the sync folder, but good luck finding it. You wish you could just sort by name and grab IMG_1002 directly, but since the names are all random you'll need to scroll through hundreds (or thousands) of thumbnails and try to figure out which picture was originally called IMG_1002.

Because of this issue, I think the sync mode is useless.

However, you can still back up your pictures in a semi-manual way. The trick is that if you do a manual copy to get a picture from the phone onto the drive, then the original file name is preserved. So, instead of doing the sync, use the manual copy mode. This isn't quite as tedious as it sounds because the app understands the problem with duplicate file names, and it gives you the opportunity to deal with them.

Here's what you do. Set up a folder on the drive where you want to backup your phone's pictures. Using the app, select all the pictures on the phone and copy them to this folder. Let's say you have 500 pictures. The copy will take a while, but you will eventually have all 500 pictures in that folder on the drive. Then a few days later, you want to backup your newer pictures, but you aren't sure exactly which ones are new. Do the same thing you did originally. Using the app, select all the pictures on the phone, and tell the app to copy them to that same folder. After thinking about it for a while, it will tell you that you have selected 541 pictures to copy, but 500 of them have duplicate file names. It will ask you what you want to do about that. Select the "skip" option, and any file with a duplicate file name won't get copied. In this example, it will only copy the 41 pictures that weren't there before.

This works, but it's still not great. It takes a while to analyze the files before starting the copy. Let's say you had 1000 pictures originally, and you only took 2 new ones. The backup should be fast, right? Well, no. It takes the app a surprisingly long time to analyze the 1002 pictures and figure out that 1000 of them have duplicate file names. Eventually, it will tell you about the 1000 duplicates and you can select "skip". Then it will copy only the 2 new pictures. But even though there were only two new pictures, the process takes a frustratingly long time.

If you know exactly which pictures are new, and there aren't very many, you can always just pick those by hand instead of doing the select-all. In that case, the process is very fast since the app is only dealing with the few pictures you selected and not analyzing a 1000 of them.
text_fidelity_b: SanDisk iXpand 16GB Mobile Flash Drive with Lightning Connector for iPhones, iPads & Computers (SDIX-016G-G57)

text_fidelity_a:
GAOMON PD2200 130% sRGB Full-Laminated Pen Display with 8192 Battery-Free Tilt-Support Stylus 8 Touch Buttons -21.5'' Graphics Drawing Tablet Monitor with Adjustable Stand I am a huge supporter of open source graphics software because I feel that the leading brand name software uses their virtual monopoly to bully people into overpriced, restrictive, nonsensical subscription programs. When I saw that this tablet was listed as being compatible with GIMP and most other graphics programs, I felt comfortable purchasing it for my uses.

However, upon installing it, I found that it is not actually compatible with the vast majority of graphic software except for those supported by Adobe, and a couple of other inferior programs. To clarify, it will still "function" with most programs, but only as a basic mouse. It will not support pressure sensitivity nor tilt. This, in my mind, means that it is NOT compatible, as pressure and tilt are essential functions for any illustrator. Without them, this is basically just a glorified mouse pad.

From Gaomon's troubleshooting website regarding lack of pressure sensitivity:

"The version of your drawing program might be too low to support pen pressure. Please upload it or try to draw in other drawing programs. Here do we suggest you some drawing programs. For windows system: Adobe Photoshop CC, Adobe Photoshop CC 2015, Adobe Photoshop CC 2017, Adobe Photoshop CC 2018, Adobe Photoshop cs5，Adobe Photoshop cs6, Adobe Animate CC2017 For Mac system: Adobe Photoshop CC, Adobe Photoshop CC 2015, Adobe Photoshop CC 2017, Adobe Photoshop cs5, Adobe Photoshop cs6, Adobe illustrator cs6, Adobe Flash Professional CC, Adobe Animate CC 2018 Other free drawing programs: Sai, Krita, FireAlpaca"

Contrast that with the information in the product listing, which says, "compatible with most of major drawing software such as Photoshop、SAI version 2、Illustrator、krita、firealpaca、gimp、SketchBook Pro、MediBang Paint Pro, etc."

GIMP and others are clearly listed, but are not actually compatible. This is highly misleading.

As for other aspects of the tablet, I can't say too much as I haven't used it very much due to this issue. However, from what I have found so far, the display looks good, and the set up is pretty straightforward, although their manual is extremely confusing to try to follow.

The buttons on the side of the display are completely smooth and can not be felt; there is nothing there to help you locate them by tactile means, so you will have to stop looking at your work and visually find them in order to use them. They are also located such that they are easily pressed accidentally when adjusting the position of your tablet, which gets annoying pretty quickly.

The chords that come with the tablet are a bit short, maybe 4 or 5 feet, which doesn't allow for much room to position your tablet if you use a PC that is located beneath your desk or to the side, especially if the hook-up ports are on the back of the PC. You can of course buy replacement chords.

The stylus is very lightweight, which I personally consider a positive but some people may prefer a heftier stylus.

There is not much lag when using the stylus; the movement is smooth enough for my needs. The pressure sensitivity, when tested in a diagnostic program, seems quite good as well. It just doesn't work with the software I hoped to use it with.

Overall the tablet is a nice size and has a nice display, but the other issues are factors you should consider when deciding between this tablet and a more expensive brand.
text_fidelity_b: GAOMON PD2200 130% sRGB Full-Laminated Pen Display with 8192 Battery-Free Tilt-Support Stylus 8 Touch Buttons -21.5'' Graphics Drawing Tablet Monitor with Adjustable Stand

text_fidelity_a:
ANGELS HORN Turntable, Vinyl Record Player, Built-in Phono Preamp, Belt Drive 2-Speed, Adjustable Counterweight, AT-3600L (Upgraded Bluetooth Version) [[VIDEOID:1be91bfc02339bd396543d05da1fee38]] There are SO many things about the Angel's Horn turntable that impress me. But, first, you need to be a true audiophile to appreciate the way this turntable was designed and built.

Gone are the days of the automatic turntable, where you just drop on a stack of records and walk away. Those things were the WORST! Sure, you were free to do other things for longer periods of time. But, they were very harmful to your records. A true collector would NOT even consider having one of those things.

First, the body of the turntable is ONE SOLID PIECE OF OAK! No particle board, no hollow box, no cheap crap!

Then, there is the direct one-belt drive, no multiple gears or belts. And the motor has ONE job, the turntable. Changing the records and setting the tonearm are YOUR job, as is true with any turntable worth it's status as 'top of the line' with this one.

Now, the tonearm is another factor. As we all know, too much pressure on the record (or too little) can affect the quality of the sound, not to mention the wear on the vinyl. And, vinyl is a fragile medium, revered as one of the best sources of true stereophonic sound. We vinyl fans collect the best recordings and do everything we can to preserve that quality. When we play our records, we do so with love and care. The tonearm on this turntable is built just for us. It's counterweight is perfect, allowing us to adjust the balance to a microgram. I've not found a tonearm with a more accurate adjustment as this one.

The ability to switch between input types is a nice feature. Some of us prefer to provide our own preamps, allowing us further tweaking of the sound quality. I do. Thank you.

The dust cover is great for those that have their turntable out on top. I have mine contained within my entertainment center and opted to leave it off.

I am VERY happy with my Angel's Horn turntable and very happy to give it five stars.
text_fidelity_b: ANGELS HORN Turntable, Vinyl Record Player, Built-in Phono Preamp, Belt Drive 2-Speed, Adjustable Counterweight, AT-3600L (Upgraded Bluetooth Version)

NETGEAR Orbi Compact Wall-Plug Whole Home Mesh WiFi System - WiFi router and wall-plug satellite extender with speeds up to 2.2 Gbps over 3,500 sq. feet, AC2200 (RBK20W) This is an updated version of a mesh system router and satellite I already have. The technology is great when it's working, but, for whatever reason, my system has needed to be reset once a week or more, and the coverage is nowhere near as good as it claims it should be.

My hope was that the newer version would be faster and have better coverage. It isn't. It doesn't. And, like the earlier version, it has to be in AP mode to work with my FIOS modem (FIOS has a version of this available with its own firmware, but you have to buy a new one, and it won't work with any other ISP). Those hopes dashed, my next hope was that I could at least use the router as a satellite on my existing system, which, of course not.

So, you would think I could at LEAST use the satellite from the new one with the old system or the old satellite with the new one? They are the same model, after all. And that, too, would be a nope.

What I finally did, after hours on the internet (and other hours just trying to set up the new one by itself - it was the same with the old one - it for some reason despises custom settings and will not save them the first many times. It will also lose them after firmware upgrades, I expect, like its predecessor), was set it up alongside the old one with its own network name. Now I have one network serving one side of the house and the other serving the other. Speeds are good. So far, no routing issues, and I don't really expect any. The two network solution seems to have worked well for others.

But really.

If you are looking to expand your Orbi network, check out the nighthawk mesh expanders. I have the 7500, and it's excellent. Also, don't take my lukewarm review for a no-rec. The Orbi is, as far as I can tell from personal experience, buggy and locked down, but, again from personal experience, it beats the Velop (its nearest competitor) by a mile for coverage.
text_fidelity_b: NETGEAR Orbi Compact Wall-Plug Whole Home Mesh WiFi System - WiFi router and wall-plug satellite extender with speeds up to 2.2 Gbps over 3,500 sq. feet, AC2200 (RBK20W)

First the things I like about this Camcorder:
This camcorder records in high definition (1020 at 30 fps), and two low resolution (720P at both 30 and 60 fps) select-able from the screen.
There is a option for setting the camera up for motion control triggered recording.
The system has a IR based night vision system to record in total blackout conditions.
The remote can be used to control most modes of the camcorder and start/stop recording.
This system comes with a external mic to help in recording the audio component of your filming, you have the option to use this mic or not depending on your circumstances.
You can use the camcorder as a photo camera with resolutions ranging from 5mp to 24mp along with settings for white balance, color, and shutter speeds.
You can turn off the beep sound for camera functions, something you may use if recording wildlife.
This Camcorder comes with a wide view lens, great when recording in a shallow area such as a room to get everyone and everything into one shot.
Extra battery, handy for extended use or areas where you cannot recharge the camera.

Things I would like to see improved:
The zoom is digital only, not an optical zoom. This limits the camcorder to recording only items in a shallow depth, not great for outdoor use unless you are up close to your subject.

All in all, a decent camcorder for use where you are close (physically) to your subject, or as long as you understand its limitations.

text_fidelity_a:
TP-LINK TL-PA511 KIT AV500 Powerline Gigabit Adapter Starter Kit, up to 500Mbps The TP-Link Powerline Adapter is a great kit for spanning distances or to help boost the signal of a router in the home. What this does is take the signal from your modem or router and transmits it over your power lines, and this allows you to have signal where you might otherwise have environmental issues blocking a wireless signal such as concrete, steel beams or just distance. One of the major drawbacks to this product is that the plugs you are using must be on the same circuit, though most people shouldn't run into this issue.

One of the biggest issues I have with this product is the fact that it isn't plug and play, not by the true definition. You HAVE to run the software to get your computer to recognize the plugs. I attempted to use them without running the software first and my computer couldn't connect to my home network. After running the software, it connected no problem. So Please take note: THIS IS NOT TRUE PLUG AND PLAY.

These are Gigabit (please note "Gigabit" is not the same as "Gigabyte") adapters and work very well. I was able to watch Youtube.com and Hulu without any issues. The web pages loaded as quickly as if I were directly connected to my router or on my wifi network.

Pros:

-Great for Larger houses to get a better signal for the home network.
-Good for streaming and downloads.
-Creates a good enough connection to act as if you are directly connected to the modem/router.

Cons:

-MUST be on the same circuit!
-Can't use a surge strip or UPS(uninterruptable power source) with these adapters so there is a risk of electrical shock to your computer during a storm.
-NOT TRUE Plug and Play. YOU MUST RUN THE SOFTWARE FIRST.

3.5 stars
text_fidelity_b: TP-LINK TL-PA511 KIT AV500 Powerline Gigabit Adapter Starter Kit, up to 500Mbps

I always like my electronics to have buttons and especially my kindle since I tend to read with one thumb on the screen itself I worried that if I upgraded to this, my thumb would either end up turning pages too soon or it wouldn't be sensitive enough to read my thumb when I wanted to. My old kindle no longer took a charge after 6 years so I had to upgrade and literally the only reason I went with this over anything else (I was wanting to get another one of my old kindles) was the backlight. I have insomnia so I'm often awake in bed with my snoring boyfriend next to me so having a light on isn't an option so having a kindle with a backlight would be ideal.

Turns out my worry over not having a button was all in vain! The touch screen has just the right amount of sensitivity. It's not so sensitive that resting my thumb on the screen where it's comfortable activates anything, but it's not so dull that I can't turn the pages easily. The back lighting is adjustable so I don't have to blind myself and I don't have to use it if I don't want to if I've got plenty of natural light. The screen is clear and crisp, it fits comfortably in my hand and the amount of books I can fit on there is insane! I've currently got 200 titles and I've still got plenty of room for more. It moves faster than my old kindle and the charge is amazing. I've been using it for over a month now and I'm still at 25% battery without charging it once aside from the day I received it.

This is by far the best kindle I've ever had!

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Lighted Leather Cover, Burgundy Red (Fits Kindle Keyboard) I don't know if I'd have bought this for myself sight unseen because I'm pretty much a cheapskate unless I know that spending more actually means better quality. I don't buy things just for the labels.

My husband bought me a Kindle and this cover for Christmas and I am in love with both. The case is obviously well made throughout. The leather and binding are solid. The material on the inside covers is lovely to the touch and, not being slick, it offers a little resistance to slipping if you are resting it on another cloth-covered surface like an overstuffed chair arm.

I often read in bed in the dark and love the way the cover works here. At some angles there's a bit of a flare of light on the screen closest to the light, but a little adjustment fixes that. It's tens times easier than wrestling with a paperbound book and an attached book light.

I find that I take my Kindle out of the cover fairly often to play games or do anything much with the key pad. The first day or so I scared myself by not lining it up quite properly and having the top hinge engaged while the bottom one was only part of the way hooked in. I just patiently and gently worked it till the top hinge disengaged and made a mental note to pay a little attention when I slip the Kindle onto the hinges.

Great product.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Lighted Leather Cover, Burgundy Red (Fits Kindle Keyboard)

The bass lacks strength and intensity, while the treble and mid feel a bit canned, and there's an overall lack of definition.

Are these bad? No. They're better than many headphones, and are ok for the price. But for a little more money, you can do much better. Still, if this is the price range you want, and the environment is a priority for you, as well as supporting businesses that try to be responsible, it is worth considering these.

Back to “battery vs brightness”
- when it’s all said and done, after adjustments, I get in a full movie (2.5 hours) with no issue.
- if you go low brightness in pitch black, you might get closer to claimed stats.

text_fidelity_a:
woednx Smart Watch,1.4''Full Touch Fitness Tracker with Heart Rate,Blood Pressure and Sleep Monitor,Message Notification,Smartwatch for Men WomenIP68 Waterproof Smartwatch Sports for iOS Android-Blue PROS

1. The silicone band is very comfortable. Apparently if it breaks, it can be replaced, though I’m not sure where or how you would buy a new band.

2. The appearance is sleek and modern, and the size of the watch face makes the digital numbers easy to read.

3. It has a rechargeable battery, which may have a longer life than the non-rechargeable batteries of most sports watches.

4. If you want a smart watch that is far cheaper than most brands, this might work for you.

CONS

1. There are three primary functions that I use a sports watch for: to instantly check the time, a stopwatch, and a timer. It irritated me no end with this watch that, after only a few seconds of being lit up, its face goes dark. While this might save the charge on the rechargeable battery, there are plenty of times when my right hand it not free to punch the button on this watch to light up its face, and I can’t quickly and conveniently check the time! It is also a hassle trying to use the stopwatch and timer functions.

2. I absolutely loathe the way this watch’s battery is recharged. Instead of using a standard C cable, the charging cable attaches magnetically, and it becomes detached far too easily. There is also no warning when the battery of this watch is about to go dead.

3. I don’t like the software this phone uses. It is a major hassle to learn for what I personally consider very little useful return. Why? Because most of the functions offered by this watch that are of any interest to me I can get through my smartphone. I use my phone and a Bluetooth for phone calls, texting, music, and hearing alarms. I check the weather by looking around me when outside or looking at weather apps on my phone. I use my phone for photography.
The rest of the functions this watch offers I personally find to be useless. I do not need a watch to tell me how to do a deep breathing exercises. As a healthy individual with no heart issues, I do not need to monitor my heart rate 24/7. (And if I did, I would use medical equipment that is far more reliable than this cheap watch.) I don’t need to obsessively monitor my sleep. (And, again, if I did, I wouldn’t trust this cheap watch to do an accurate job of it.)

4. Its pedometer function might have been of use to me, but unfortunately, it is inaccurate.

CONCLUSION

I dumped this watch and went back to a regular, inexpensive sports watch.
text_fidelity_b: woednx Smart Watch,1.4''Full Touch Fitness Tracker with Heart Rate,Blood Pressure and Sleep Monitor,Message Notification,Smartwatch for Men WomenIP68 Waterproof Smartwatch Sports for iOS Android-Blue

text_fidelity_a:
Belkin Grip Candy Sheer Case for iPhone 5 and 5S (Purple and Turquoise) This is the second case I have gotten that I could not give a good rating because of the bottom part, which does not fit with the adapter (to allow older devices to work with the new iPhone), and it does not fit most professional cables that go into the headphone jack.
Because my car has a built-in charger and system that plays with i-technology (previous generations), I HAVE to use the adapter, not just the new wire. Because I am a dancer and instructor and use my phone for job every day, I HAVE to have a case that lets me plug into our system. For those reasons, this case, like the last one I got, is useless to me.

Could you peel back the case to leave the bottom exposed? Yes. But over time, this warps the plastic and creates a loose fit, and putting it on and taking if off can cause the screen protector to come off around the edges.

Could you cut part of the bottom to allow the adapter and wires to fit? No. The plastic is thick enough that the wire will still not fit the headphone jack. As for the adapter, it might fit, but it will want to come out because the thickness, again, will make it want to separate.

So far, the only case to fit my iPhone is a pretty cheap import that has very thin plastic and is generally not a great case either. Is it a design problem with the phone as well? Maybe, but the people making cases should take that into account and design something that works with the iPhone 5 as it is, not as we wish it were. I guess I'm keeping my brand X case a bit longer.
text_fidelity_b: Belkin Grip Candy Sheer Case for iPhone 5 and 5S (Purple and Turquoise)

text_fidelity_a:
Anker Ergonomic Optical USB Wired Vertical Mouse 1000/1600 DPI, 5 Buttons CE100 It takes some getting used to. I have three of these Anker ergos. Two are wireless and are in use at work. One is wired and on my gaming rig at home.

Gaming: My normal mouse is a Logitech gaming mouse which had been my go to for many years. It was fast accurate and had plenty of built in controls for everything I needed. This mouse also has all of the relevant controls and the resolution button is less likely to get accidentally hit than on the Logitech. It does still get hit here and there though. I also find that the vertical style while more comfortable is not as ideal for gaming but honestly speaking is a small niggle in that the comfort is far more appreciated than the slightly awkward hand position (as movements need to be very fast). Is this up to par with other premium gaming controllers? I have my doubts, but it is certainly comfortable and as a wired controller is adequate for sure.

Everyday: Just yes. Especially considering the value. It is both affordable as an ergonomic mouse and comfortable. You may need to make adjustments to your seating angle as the tendency is for this mouse to be most comfortable when your forearm is almost flat on the desk surface.

Look and feel: It is not an especially heavy mouse. But it does have a level of refinement expected on something more costly. It is also well designed and not obscenely gaudy like a lot of products these days. The rubbery matte surface is pleasant and tactile and the buttons are responsive and easy to actuate. The mouse is somewhat full-sized. I don't want to say large because I have small-medium hands and I can use this just fine, but by no means do I have small hands. Those who have small hands might find this more of a challenge to use though I don't doubt you'll get used to it. The primary buttons and grip would be fine, but the locations of the scroll wheel and the forward nav button are a bit of a reach.

Like I said I have three of these in various formats and love them all. Other than my ultra compact travel mouse, these are used on all of my home and work devices. At such a reasonable cost you can't lose by at least trying it.
text_fidelity_b: Anker Ergonomic Optical USB Wired Vertical Mouse 1000/1600 DPI, 5 Buttons CE100

text_fidelity_a:
Jawbone Big JAMBOX Wireless Bluetooth Speaker - Graphite Hex - Retail Packaging The first thing I noticed when I opened the box was how small the Big Jambox is. It's truly portable and the name is more accurate of its sound quality. The first thing I noticed when I turned on the unit was that it talked to me and charted out the steps to pair the speaker to the iPhone 5. The second thing I noticed was the sound. The big full sound. I have truly eclectic tastes. My music collection includes rock, blues, jazz, world music from Africa, the Middle East, and the Lapland of Norway. I listen to didgeridoos from Australia, fiddles, marimbas, and jaw harps from Kyrzykstan. The quality is so good Im a bit blown away by the technology. The clarity is a wonder when listening to vocal qualities of choir ensembles, Bobbie McFerrin, , solo clarinets, and horn sections as well as my favorite twangy African and Middle Eastern instruments. The bass is great considering the speakers size. I predict I will enjoy my symphonic classical music more from now on.
But be reasonable, put it in perspective. Don't expect your Big Jambox to take the place of the power of a live stadium U2 concert or the knock-you -on-your-ass sound wall that passes through your body from a live large brass section of a jazz band orchestra, or be loud enough to overwhelm 10 or 20 loud drunk party goers. Don't be a bonehead! It flabberghasts me that anyone would criticize this speaker. If you actually listen to the sound quality of singers and instruments, or enjoy deep full sounds, spend the money (im on the cheap side) and get the Big Jambox. And dats da facts Jack.
text_fidelity_b: Jawbone Big JAMBOX Wireless Bluetooth Speaker - Graphite Hex - Retail Packaging

FYHXele Computer Monitor, Gaming Monitor 24 Inch 75Hz, IPS FHD 1080P, 2xHDMI, USB Type-C, Built-in Speakers, Adaptive Sync, VESA for Office Home, Black I’ve been using the FYHXele 24 Inch Monitor (75Hz version) for the last month, and it has totally spoiled me for playing games on my Switch! The monitor has built-in speakers, so I can hear a game’s music while playing. It’s a small but nice feature; I can easily switch the input from my laptop to my Switch and not have to rearrange my whole desk to play games.

The picture is bright and vibrant. I’ve been playing Hades for the last month and it looks SO good on this screen. Bright and crisp, even if I play during the day. I also use the monitor as a second display for work, it’s good for that too, either as a streaming display or for text and spreadsheets.

I use it with my MacBook Pro, the monitor has 2 HDMI inputs and 1 USB-C. The USB-C port doesn’t support passthrough charging.

A VESA plate is included, which was a nice plus. I do use a monitor arm because I don’t like the stand this monitor comes with. The angle and height are not adjustable at all, and I didn’t like the default angle. The base is 9 inches by 7 inches, so it has a large footprint. I also don’t love the “FYHXele” printed in white at the bottom of the screen.

The power cable is relatively short, only 50 inches. It’s an AC adapter, not a power brick. The box also includes an HDMI cable -- another nice plus -- but unfortunately my cable had a cut in the coating, so I could see the copper wire.

Overall, I think this is a decent budget monitor. I never want to play my Switch in handheld mode anymore, the picture quality has spoiled me that much. The dual HDMI inputs make it easy to switch between work and fun; I’ve also used this as a Discord display, rotated 90° on a VESA arm.
text_fidelity_b: FYHXele Computer Monitor, Gaming Monitor 24 Inch 75Hz, IPS FHD 1080P, 2xHDMI, USB Type-C, Built-in Speakers, Adaptive Sync, VESA for Office Home, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Plantronics M110 Mobile Headband Headset (45628-51) I think this is a great headset for the money. I can wear it comfortably for hours. The volume is good. I rarely get complaints from listeners, and when I do, a small movement of the microphone boom fixes it right up.

I own or use 5 headsets. The only headset of the 5 which I have found to be better is the expensive Plantronics I use at work. Of the 4 I have at home, 2 are the "wrap around the ear" kind. I do not find this style comfortable. I cannot wear them for more than about 30 minutes. text_fidelity_a:
Toshiba TransMemory Pro USB 3.0 Flash Drive (PFU064U-1BDS) With its huge 64GB file storage capacity, this flash drive can theoretically store the entire contents of a PC's hard drive and its operating system. Since I don't have that many files to store on an everyday basis, I am reserving this flash drive to store high-resolution videos and other RAM-eating monster files.

For $80, this is rather overpriced. There are USB drives that are cheaper and will do the job just as well. To make the USB look like it's worth the extra price, Toshiba made the casing unnecessarily oversized - there's no practical reason why the USB case had to be so wide (you will have trouble sticking another USB drive next to it, which is annoying). It's a gimmick to impress the user, nothing more. However, when you hold it in your hand, it's not as heavy as the metallic finish would lead you to believe - it's actually very lightweight, and to be honest, feels cheap. I have questions of its durability, despite the fancy advertising.

To test, I copied all the videos I had stored in my PC to see how fast it would be to store all of them on this monster drive. I was disappointed that the saving time was not noticeably faster, which may not be the fault of the USB drive but rather my computer. However, I have to say it was a relief that I never got the "you don't have enough memory" message, so you can count on this USB to store tons of videos you can't find room for elsewhere.

The only drawback to this single-USB method of storage is that I don't feel entirely comfortable saving so much stuff on just ONE drive, despite its capacity. It's equivalent to putting all your eggs in one basket - what if you lose that single USB - you're screwed. Though convenient, I'd rather spread out my back-up files, so if you use this USB to save a huge file, I'd buy more than one just to be safe.

The other thing I thought was unnecessary was the included encryption software that's included on the drive. You only see it when you open up the Files folder, and there are two lengthy PDFs with instructions on how to activate the password and security options. Fortunately you do not require to activate them in order to use the drive - I've never found I needed such security measures, but if you plan to store financial data on this USB, it's a good feature.

Lastly, I hate the fact that, unlike my other drives, it has a cap. I am forever losing the caps to my flash drives and have since opted to buy only the retractable ones, where you can slide the connector in or out. Too bad this one doesn't have it, otherwise I would have added a star.

So, in short, a mixed review. Give me a drive that's cheaper, that's big on the inside but small on the outside, capless, and I'd buy more of them.
text_fidelity_b: Toshiba TransMemory Pro USB 3.0 Flash Drive (PFU064U-1BDS)

text_fidelity_a:
KZ ZS10 Pro, Linsoul 4BA+1DD 5 Driver in Ear Monitor, HiFi Metal Earphones, with Stainless Steel Faceplate, 2 Pin Detachable Cable (Without Mic, Black) Best sounding in-ear headphones I've ever heard, by a mile. I've owned the Bang and Olufsen H3, Sony XBA H1, Klipsch S4, X7, X6i, 1More Dual Drivers, Beats by Dr Dre Tour (wired), and Monster Cable's Jamz and Turbines.

The bass has lots of range and goes DEEP, in some tracks it even reminds me of my Kicker CVR 12' car subwoofer I used to blast about 15 years ago. It is not quite that overpowering, of course, and it balances out nicely with the other frequencies. The midrange is very present and natural sounding judging by how vocals and guitar strings sound. The highs are beautiful, they sound very accurate to me and present no sibilance. The overall sound is very rich and detailed, it allows you to follow specific instruments as you listen, and it even presents some soundstage (which I didn't think was possible in in-ears, maybe my aforementioned B&O H3 had some)

Overall these do have a V sound signature with boosted bass and treble, but not as marked as almost everything else that's in the market. In order to eliminate any fatigue caused by this, I would strongly recommend that you disable any bass boost, make sure you're not elevating bass or treble at all in EQ, and go even deeper and disable default features like Dolby Atmos (Oneplus phone) and even the Hi Fi quad DAC on LG phones (which I've found does introduce a bit of a V curve itself)

Other than their sound these earphones' build quality seems very good and durable. I'm in disbelief they could cost $60. You're welcome
text_fidelity_b: KZ ZS10 Pro, Linsoul 4BA+1DD 5 Driver in Ear Monitor, HiFi Metal Earphones, with Stainless Steel Faceplate, 2 Pin Detachable Cable (Without Mic, Black)

text_fidelity_a:
ViewSonic VA2359-SMH 23 Inch IPS 1080p LED Monitor with HDMI and VGA Inputs What I like about this monitor:
1. Easy to set up - I used my previous monitor video cable and power cord and had it up and running in a few minutes.
2. Very clear resolution despite having an old video card.
3. It has an HDMI connection but I am using the regular VGA input and it still very clear.
4. A VGA and sound cord are included.
5. Very sleek, streamline black design which goes nicely with my other computer accessories.

What could be better:
1. The included instructions tell you nothing about how to make video and audio adjustments. I can't use a bright setting and it took a good while to figure out how to use the buttons underneath the screen. They are not intuitive at all.
2. Poor Audio - if you want good audio from this monitor that will not be possible. It is a thin monitor and the audio is very thin and tinny. I was hoping I could disconnect my external sound system to make more room on my desk but found out that I must keep it if I want to hear any decent sound from my computer.
3. While testing the volume on this monitor you must still figure out how to toggle using the various buttons underneath. There is no single volume button or toggle switch. And it will not get very loud.
4. If you don't bump the monitor or use the toggle switches the monitor stays fairly steady on it's stand. Otherwise it will rock and jiggle while using the buttons.
5. No HDMI cable is included.

The scant instructions did say to visit their website to download the latest drivers but as of yet this monitor is not listed in their driver drop down window. I don't think that matter much at this time as the monitor is very clear and sharp.
Overall: Good monitor for the price (as of this review it costs $138.24 Prime) which I feel is a fair price.
text_fidelity_b: ViewSonic VA2359-SMH 23 Inch IPS 1080p LED Monitor with HDMI and VGA Inputs

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Fire TV - 1st Generation UPDATED March 11, 2015--See Below

SHOULD YOU BUY THIS UNIT?
In my opinion, this unit, like all things Amazon, is only about 80% ready for market but they release this stuff anyway. It's a cheap shot to their customers and they should straighten up and actually release products when they have all the features advertised actually implemented.

Buy this thing only if USB isn't important to you AND if you are willing to wait hours to upload video and picture content to the Amazon Cloud Drive. ABOUT THE CLOUD DRIVE--the initial allocation of space for your account is only a few gigs (I think 2 gigs). After that you can upgrade and pay Amazon more money for the bump up in storage space. That this unit has a non-functioning, flaccid USB forces you to use their cloud for video streaming your own stuff and this works for Amazon because lots of folks will end up paying for more cloud storage. This is borderline unethical in my opinion.

Pros:
Sets up easily.
Great help videos
Outstanding picture quality
WiFi and Wired connections both very good
Small footprint

Cons:
USB not implemented so you cannot play your own video content without uploading to their cloud
Uploading to their Cloud takes much longer than other clouds (Dropbox for example). It's hours compared to minutes
Puny cloud storage allocation without upgrade
Search has no QWERTY layout to type in your search and no way to add a space and second or more words to the search
Limited on-line support

CONCLUSION: Not really ready for prime time if you need full functionality in a unit like this.

UPDATED March 11, 2015: REDUCING THIS TO TWO STARS. Okay, this is the most annoying, frustrating and unreliable piece of technology I've ever purchased. In the months since I bought this item its performance has degraded to where it is simply unacceptable. Amazon tech support is of little help and neither is Netflix tech support. Here are the NEW FEATURES my Fire TV now performs:

1) Regularly pauses an in-progress program as if I'd pressed the pause button. It usually resumes after I press the play button on the remote.
2) It does not play nice with Netflix and often (actually daily) gets hung so that I see an error message telling me there's trouble, "playing this video right now...," and suggests I try later or pick something different. Well, I don't want to wait, nor do I wish to watch something else.
3) It often cannot find my HDMI cable, even though I've tried several cables. It is, therefore, not a cable problem but an internal glitch in the Fire TV box.
4) Often after turning it on, it goes to a blank screen from which there is no return.
5) There are many more fun things this piece of garbage does but why bother list them.

Tomorrow, I'm going to Best Buy to pick up a Roku 3 for about what it sells for on Amazon. See, then I won't have to wait for it to be shipped and, if necessary, I can take it back to a real store and exchange or return it. Oh, and I intend to donate this Fire TV box to the garbage can. I do hope it won't offend the garbage man/woman/person/whatever.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Fire TV - 1st Generation

text_fidelity_a:
Jaybird X4 Wireless Bluetooth Headphones for Sport Fitness and Running, Compatible with iOS and Android Smartphones: Sweatproof and Waterproof - Black Metallic/Flash These are very good Bluetooth earbuds for sports use. Construction is very lightweight, but still very durable. Earpieces are very secure when I'm running or working out at the gym and more than comfortable enough for hour-long workouts. Sound quality is pretty good out-of-the-box, but a little thin at the higher frequencies (especially noticeable with acoustic music). Fortunately, Jaybird has a great smartphone app you can use to equalize the sound. I was never very good at designing my own equalization profiles by ear, but the app has several ready made profiles so I just picked the one that sounded best with my favorite music (boosting higher frequencies more than lower frequencies). There is no noise cancellation, but noise isolation is very good with the included foam eartips (not the default eartips).

I really do not like that you need a special dongle to recharge this headset. You can't just plug a standard USB cable directly into these, like with most Bluetooth headset. This may have something to do with the headset's waterproof rating, but other headsets I own are also waterproof and can still be recharged with a standard cable. I am concerned that the proprietary charging dongle will get lost or broken or I will just forget to bring it with me when traveling.
text_fidelity_b: Jaybird X4 Wireless Bluetooth Headphones for Sport Fitness and Running, Compatible with iOS and Android Smartphones: Sweatproof and Waterproof - Black Metallic/Flash

text_fidelity_a: SABRENT USB 3.0 Tool Free Enclosure for 2.5” and 3.5” Internal SATA Hard Drives (EC-KSL3) I was all set to return this because it would not recognize my Seagate 4TB SSHD. In disk management it showed up as GPT protective partition. After googling, I found that the only way to get past this was to use Diskpart and Clean the drive--that meant wiping out everything on the drive. Since I had already cloned it, I went ahead and used the Clean command and wiped it out. Still couldn't do anything with the drive in disk management. So using Diskpart again, I used the command, Create Partition Primary. At this point, Diskpart couldn't do anything else. It would not create a volume to format, so I had to use Disk Management to create the volume and format it to exFat. I should state that the drive was recognized by my computer internally when it was connected to a Sata port, but once it was put into the Sabrent, it's drive information was changed and made unusable until I performed the procedure above. Not sure why this happened, maybe because it's a SSHD, but I kinda doubt it since I had no problems with the drive when connected to a Sata Port.
text_fidelity_b: SABRENT USB 3.0 Tool Free Enclosure for 2.5” and 3.5” Internal SATA Hard Drives (EC-KSL3)

text_fidelity_a:
Bose SoundTouch 10 wireless speaker, works with Alexa - Black Before writing this review I glanced over some reviews of earlier models, and whatever issues previous editions of the Bose SoundTouch speakers may have had seem to have been worked out with this SoundTouch 10.

Setup was simple with the SoundTouch app (available for iOS, Android, and Kindle Fire devices). We had the speaker set up and operating in less than 5 minutes using an iPad. You'll need your home network security code to connect to WiFi and that's about it.

It comes with a remote, but most of the controlling is done from your device (tablet or phone). The remote is handy for adjusting the volume when you're using your device for other things.

The speaker is about the size of a cereal box. The sound that comes out is impressive for its size. I think there's a wee bit of case resonance in the mid range, but that's just me -- everyone else thinks it sounds terrific. It doesn't rival a huge stereo system but it's really, really good.

Now excuse me while I get on my soapbox about monaural. This is a single speaker system, not stereo, and that, to me, is a good thing. I'm a fan of monaural. It solves a lot of issues about speaker placement (trying to make sure they're equally distant), and you hear the full mix as the producers and artists intended. You can move anywhere around the room and not have half the mix disappear. And if you like oldies, particularly from the 1960s, this fixes the problems caused by common pan/mix practices from that era (for example, drums and bass panned hard left, guitars and backup singers panned hard right, lead vocals in the middle). If you listen to mixes like that in headphones, you pretty much have to mix the music down in your imagination since bass/drums are exclusively in one ear and keyboards in the other. Some devices don't support mono audio output (I'm looking at you, Windows phone), and as far as I know no one makes a dual-ear mono headset for phones either. So a mono speaker solves the issue. Okay, that's it for the soapbox. Back to the review.

The only tone control available in the Bose app is bass volume. But since the sound is well engineered, it's adequate. And bass is very audible. Not subwoofer level audible, but it's very present.

The SoundTouch app itself is impressive. It really does make setup a breeze. And the listening options are VAST. Hundreds of radio stations from around the world on WiFi, streaming music services, Pandora, Spotify, and so forth. I used to do a little shortwave listening, and if you're a DXer, this exceeds the capability of SW by far, and every station is digitally clear. And you can connect directly to play music straight from your device.

Just to be clear, the speaker itself needs a wall outlet to power it. It's not battery powered. But everything else is wireless. More speakers can be added, but it's so easily unplugged and moved around that one speaker can easily be sufficient.

Nice product from Bose.
text_fidelity_b: Bose SoundTouch 10 wireless speaker, works with Alexa - Black

text_fidelity_a:
D-Link Wi-Fi Camera with Remote Viewing (DCS-930L) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I loved how simple it was to get this set up and working. I just followed the instructions and it connected to my home wireless network without a hiccup. The image quality is OK. Decent for a basic webcam. Good enough for my purposes.

GOOD:
Simple to set up and get working.
Quality is adequate
Cheap!
Multiple cameras work well. Just different tabs for different cameras on the web view.
iPhone App: Great! Also very easy to use. Watching your camera(s) on the iPhone is actually easier a less glitchy than watching on the PC.

BAD:
Pretty short range for the wireless. I get better wireless range with my laptop and iPhone (802.11N). I actually bought a range extender so I could connect a 2nd DCS-930L camera just 40 ft away (but through two walls).
Short power cord
Web Viewers are not so great. The remote web viewer (MyDlink) has resolution issues and Java issues. Works but you have to click an extra OK or two. And the viewer takes a few seconds to load. The "local" web view - directly through your own network - also has Java issues - prompting you to authorize the app every time you load it (it doesn't remember the authorization - at least not on my computer which is updated with the latest Java as of 6-8-13). They should really work on this. Also, it'd be nice if the viewer were more stripped down so you don't have to have a big window open. Just The Video Please.

Not only would I buy this again, but I'd buy a 2nd one. I've tried to configure other wireless cameras through the firewall, forwarding ports blah blah blah. Sometimes it works. Sometimes not. This one just works. And it has the nifty smartphone apps. In my book, for the price, that gets it 5 stars.
text_fidelity_b: D-Link Wi-Fi Camera with Remote Viewing (DCS-930L) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

1 year update: Changed 5 stars to 3.
Just before Fourth of July vacation, the fan quit responding. This is after 11 months and a half since my purchase.

I changed the cable, did not work, then cleaned the mesh that covered the fans and tried, still did not work. After coming back from vacation I consulted to store, but they could not do anything about it. Sadly Amazon did not list anywhere to contact the seller, so I could not return the item even it came with 1 year warranty. I am not going to buy item from the seller who does not list their contact information.

text_fidelity_a:
Microsoft Wireless All-In-One Media Keyboard,Black - Wireless Keyboard with Track Pad. USB Wireless Receiver. Spill Resistant Design. 2AAA Batteries Included. Most people purchase this wireless keyboard to use at home with their TV or other media setup. I actually purchased it to use at work as a more ergonomic option. No, this is not billed as an ergonomic keyboard, but the main issue I was having was reaching for the mouse, so I wanted something with a built-in trackpad. Surprisingly, there are VERY FEW options available, particularly within a reasonable price range (<50) and offered by a name brand company.

Prior to purchasing this keyboard, I tried another which featured the trackpad front and center ([[ASIN:B004KN7PZG Gear Head USB Smart Touch II Touchpad Keyboard]]). Unfortunately, that product was way too glitchy, and the size was not ideal. I thought that the center trackpad would work well given that I'm used to using one on my laptop at home (a [[ASIN:B00IPQXZ62 Dell XPS Convertible 2 in 1]], which has a near-ideal keyboard), but that did not seem to be the case. When I began looking for keyboards with a built-in trackpad on the side, this one by Microsoft seemed to be the only viable option, although I wasn't looking for wireless.

I did like that that the keyboard is Microsoft, and I like the clean look and design. Compared to the prior keyboard that I tried, this one definitely has a more comfortable feel. Although it is small, there is adequate spacing around the keys, something the prior keyboard lacked. There is no number pad--the trackpad replaces this--but as I never used this anyway, this is no loss for me. All of the keys are a nice size, including the shift keys (these are sometimes skimped upon). Unfortunately, there is no "End" key--I knew that upon purchasing, but I still miss it. What I did NOT realize is that in order to access the Function keys, you actually have to HOLD DOWN the "FN" button. This is a bit of a pain for me, as I use Refresh (F5) constantly, so this is now a 2-handed operation. This keyboard is also missing any kind of indicator for CAPS LOCK.

The trackpad is okay. I still have my mouse plugged in, and unfortunately, I find myself using it too often, as the trackpad is not completely reliable. It does accept multi-finger scrolling gestures, which is nice, and it does pretty well with simple up-down navigation; however, I have found that side-to-side is much more uneven. I do like that there is a left-hand click button on the right side of the keyboard, and I have made use of this at times. But I've also found that sometimes my palm randoming activates the trackpad when I am typing, causing the cursor to flip to a new spot on screen, which is annoying. So, at best, this has been just average.

This keyboard includes other features that I don't use--e.g., a volume control, a separate mute button (are both necessary?), home and other "hot" keys, etc. I'm assuming that these extras would be more beneficial to someone using the keyboard in a home media setting. For my needs, this keyboard has been okay. The layout is decent, although it could have been much, much better with a few minor changes. Depending on how you plan to use it, I would recommend it with reservations.
text_fidelity_b: Microsoft Wireless All-In-One Media Keyboard,Black - Wireless Keyboard with Track Pad. USB Wireless Receiver. Spill Resistant Design. 2AAA Batteries Included.

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech G13 Programmable Gameboard with LCD Display Pros:
-Easily programmed.
-Multiple game memory.
-Many, many keys = many, many programming options.
-Digital readout looks good and lets you know exactly what download you are using without reopening Logitech window.

Cons:
-Flat palm positioning is not very comfortable for gaming (and can't be adjusted). My hand tends to cramp due to its bad ergonomics when playing FPS games more than an hour.
-Keypad ergonomics are badly thought out. Key rows are positioned bowing UPWARDS (away from your fingers) instead of downwards, making quick initiation of pinky and index finger keys more difficult.
-G13 is a bit large and can't easily be slid aside when not gaming (not a big deal to me, but somewhat inconvenient).
-Friends tell me that Razer and Logitech downloads interfere with one another, so if you have a Razer mouse or keyboard this may interfere with your use of either.
-Keys are a bit too close together without easily discernible gaps in between. This too often causes my thick fingers to strike 2 keys simultaneously.
-Overpriced for what it offers.

Overall:
Programming=excellent. Ergonomics=horrible.
For me, the keypad layout and palm rest do not work together. They look like they should, but they simply do not. The device concept is quite good, but the ergonomics make it just too difficult to consistently access and manipulate keys for real-time gaming. Very disappointing to me because with Logitech's years of experience in peripherals this should put Nostromo to shame---it simply doesn't because of the badly positioned keys and faulty wrist/palm rest ergonomics.

Follow-up:
-Down from 2 to only 1 Star, and it should be ZERO Stars. This thing is good only for a paperweight to remind me of my wasted time and wasted money.
-6 months down the road and, while gaming, each and every one of my gaming profiles (I have 3) will spontaneously reset to the default profile on their own or, even worse, all the G-keys become unresponsive.
-Sometimes on computer start-up the LCD screen lights up, but no profiles appear, not even default, and no keys respond.
-Sometimes on computer start-up the unit never powers on.
-Logitech's updates do not fix the problem(s). I've deleted the entire gaming software setup and performed reinstalls ad nauseum with no permanent positive result. What's even worse is this: it acts fine for a bit after a reinstall, so you think you've corrected it, then it starts screwing up ALL OVER AGAIN.
-BIOS adjustments do not fix the problems.
-USB ports and motherboard are completely functional throughout my gaming (I've tested/monitored them as I play) and they perform perfectly as the gamepad and/or its software crashes on its own.
-It's only 6 months old, and 2 keys are mechanically non-functional (G20 and the button below the joystick). My Belkin Nostromo n52 lasted for almost 8 YEARS of gaming with no problems whatsoever, and I was gaming three times as much back then. I'd grown used to the G13 so I was willing to overlook the buttons, or blame them on myself, and work around this issue, but when the software/electrical issues began occurring quite regularly I'd run out of patience.
-Forums addressing these (as well as other) issues have found no answers or solutions, only make-shift quick-fixes.
-Numerous forums also share the information that this is happening across a variety and multitude of different computer systems/set-ups.
-Many other owners, myself included, have had additional problems with the G13 when it is used after a computer has hibernated/slept, but we all learned to live with this as one of its quirks. We now see this as an indicator of its many issues.
-Many other owners have said that the problems began occurring after 3 or more months use (I suspect that in my case this took longer as it is only occasionally used for gaming).
-Logitech customer support has denied any fault in these matters and still maintains that their pruduct and programming is NOT the cause of any of these problems, so their help line has been useless. Meanwhile, the price plummets as word spreads.
-Only thing that works for any of us is to constantly disconnect gamepad from its current USB port, reconnect it, and computer may recognize it...but this does NOT always work...sometimes requires reboot as well...and sometimes this doesn't work either...so gamepad is inoperative until it decides to come back on a reconnection or restart. This is a band-aid at best. I refuse to do this to my system over and over.

This thing is getting returned. I advise you to save your money and time by buying some other manufacturer's product.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech G13 Programmable Gameboard with LCD Display

Cable Matters DisplayPort to DVI Adapter (DP to DVI Adapter) My desktop computer has a built in graphics card on the motherboard and I added a graphics card for gaming. The graphics card has a DVI, VGA and DisplayPort outputs. I had two monitors hooked up, one to the DVI, and one to the VGA port. I had another monitor (actually a TV) which duplicated screen two using a splitter. But I wanted to use it as a third separate monitor.

I tried several things to make a third monitor work: a DVI to HDMI cable (not an active cable) didn't work - the computer never saw the third monitor. I also tried the built in graphics card on the motherboard, plugging in an HDMI cable to its port and connecting the TV. That didn't work. it seems only one graphics card can be enabled at a time; either the one on the motherboard, or the installed graphics card.

This worked. As soon as I plugged it in, going from the displayport on the graphics card to the HDMI cable, the computer saw & recognized the 3rd monitor. Now I have three separate monitors.

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Cloud Cam Security Camera, Works with Alexa What has happened to us???

Why would we --pay money-- for Big Brothe- I mean Amazon- to see into our homes 24/7? After all the smart appliance eavesdropping/conspiracy fiascos last year, and all the privacy rights and issues going on? The 'internet of things' is absolutely hackable. Do you want your home life to be observed and hacked (or deliberately watched!) any more than you want your SSN and credit card numbers being spraypainted in big, clear writing, on the side of a City Bus?

Why would YOU personally, yes you, reading these words, right now, why would YOU want cameras in your home watching you all the time?

What is it you believe about the rest of humanity that makes eternally viewing your possessions or monitoring people in your home, or being in your own home, worth PAYING for?

Seeing something doesn't make you more secure. It might help a lawyer prosecute a criminal. But it won't fix the problems that lead to crime. And it won't prevent a bad thing from happenning. It'll just provide you with a tool to witness it. In detail. Repeatedly. Remember when we all watched those towers go down, over and over for weeks, every day? Yeah. Like that. But YOUR home. Or kids. Or whatever you value enough to feel scared of losing and then feel soothed about that fear by pointing a camera at it.

Knowing your kids are home safe? Can a phone call not verify that? If they are doing somwthing you feel the need to surreptitiously watch, what does that say about your/their abilities to form healthy trust and boundaires and respect in your relationships? And if you catch them doing wrong, could you somehow prevent it from a screen? Like, what's the result of having that evidence of wrongdoing in hand? Is it actually going to be a positive to evoke the changes you seek underneath it all? Is there somethig else that could work better?

Because pointing a security camera just says "I don't trust 'x'." It's not like a baby monitor, and you're in the next room and can respond right away if the need arises. There is a LOT of far LESS INAVSIVE technologies that can accomplish most goals this system is being pitched to solve.

Do you really want to watch whatever events unfold that you might falsely feel you are 'protecting' whatever you think will be protected from, by being able to observe it from afar?

These are PRODUCTS. Designed to make profit for manufacturers. Full stop. How do they sell security? By giving the fear of insecurity to us, and then providing a 'solution.' And at such a great price! Because it's 'introduced'. They literally have introduced us to a fear you maybe we didn't even know we had.

Sure, some of us have been victims of domestic crimes, or have pets or parents or offspring to care for. But products like this only give the illusion that we're actually DOING those things.

It's a way to avoid actual doing.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Cloud Cam Security Camera, Works with Alexa

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Sense 2 Advanced Health and Fitness Smartwatch with Tools to Manage Stress and Sleep, ECG App, SpO2, 24/7 Heart Rate and GPS, Shadow Grey/Graphite, One Size (S & L Bands Included) At this point, I have had the Sense 2 for 2 days and I know at least some of my issues will likely be fixed with later software updates. First, the good. I like the form factor. The case is thin and the watch, even with the supplied band, is comfortable. Speaking of the band, as a big guy, I was overjoyed to see the inclusion of a second band that actually fit. Also, changing bands is a snap.

Overall, it seems to be relatively high quality. The battery life, so far at least has been fantastic. I am on hour 42 of wearing it after a 99% charge and it is down to 70% battery left. The screen is fairly bright and crisp. An understated advantage of the Sense 2 (and one of the reasons I switched) is that is OS and phone brand agnostic. You can use it with Apple or Android and, unlike the Galaxy Watch, there are no features locked away if you are not using the correct brand of phone.

If you are coming from a Galaxy Watch where you could customize the watch face and all sorts of other things and that is important to you, then move along. This watch will not be for you. For now, at least, there is not really much substantive you can do to individualize your user experience. That's not so great.

Also not so great is the things that are missing. There is no Google Maps at launch. Also, despite being a Google company, no support for the Google Assistant (Alexa only sadly). There is also no interface to control music on your phone if that is important to you. I found it mildly annoying, but not a deal breaker. In addition, some people will be turned off by the fact that there are features that require a Fitbit paid subscription to get, even though you get six months for free.

The real reason I bought this watch was the ECG function. I have had A Fib for a couple of years and used to use (and still do) a Kardia XL to check my rhythm. The Galaxy Watch 4 was nice because it did a reasonable single lead reading and it meant not having to carry another gizmo with me. You simply held still and put a finger on each of the side buttons. Unfortunately, when I switched from a Galaxy phone to a Pixel, I lost the ability to do an ECG.

On the Sense 2, the ECG has not been impressive. First, I have big hands and contorting my right one to get my thumb and forefinger on the corner of the glass has been a challenge at time. It often takes several tries to get it right. Second, despite confirming on both my Kardia and my Galaxy Watch, the Sense 2 will never indicate that I am in A Fib. Apparently, if your pulse goes above 120 (which mine frequently does while in A Fib) then the Sense 2 just gives up and won't really check. Even in instances where it was below 120, the Sense will not confirm. I guess we get to settle for inconclusive results instead. Given this feature was the main reason I bought the watch, it may be a deal breaker for me and I may return it for that reason. If this feature is not that important to you, then it may still be a good option.

Overall though, it may be a good option for the right person. If you care primarily about health and fitness tracking and want a good battery life, then this is a good option. At the current $300 price point, I still feel like Fitbit may be asking a little too much given the features of the other higher end options on the market.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Sense 2 Advanced Health and Fitness Smartwatch with Tools to Manage Stress and Sleep, ECG App, SpO2, 24/7 Heart Rate and GPS, Shadow Grey/Graphite, One Size (S & L Bands Included)

And Cat. 7 sounded better to me than the Cat. 5 cables I've been using forever (plus these had largely positive reviews and looked nice and like they might be a more advanced animal, with their flat cabling and their gold-plated (or at least gold-colored) plugs), so I bought a couple of these. I think it would be food for the younger set or for travel, if you don’t want to take your expensive electronics. It is a decent tablet, just not the fastest. Each person will have decide if it will be right for them, based on budget & expectations. For me, it will get used regularly.

Highly recommend these signs.
