text_fidelity_a:
Epson Home Cinema 5050UB 4K PRO-UHD 3-Chip Projector with HDR,White The 5050ube is an excellent upgrade on the Epson 5040 projector. It provides a significant upgrade on the pseudo-4k projector with an impressive 2600 lumens making it one of the brightest projectors out there easily surpassing the 1500 lumens you would get with the entry level Sony true 4K projector. One of the big upgrades is the move to 18Gbps bandwidth giving you the ability to do 4K at 60Hz. Note that you do need to have a wired connection to get the full 18Gbps -- you only get 12 if you do the wireless option that the 5050ube offers over the regular 5050ub. Even with the reduced bandwidth that you get with the wireless setup, it is a great convenience to have the ability to stream from sources without having to run a wire from the source to the actual projector.

Another great aspect of the 5050 is the motorized lens which is a feature that other more expensive true-4k projectors do not offer. Of course with Epson you do get exceptional HDR quality as well as amazing black.

This is an impressive pseudo-4K projector that provides features that are not even found in some entry level true 4K projectors. If you are not absolutely dying to get true 4k, then this should be one of the projectors you should consider.
text_fidelity_b: Epson Home Cinema 5050UB 4K PRO-UHD 3-Chip Projector with HDR,White

The enclosed instructions with the mouse were very clear, and I had no problems setting it up and getting my computer to recognize it.  Setup was quick, too. The only thing I don't really like about this mouse is that it doesn't fit very well in my hand.  Either this mouse is too big or my hand is too small.  My hand gets cramps rather quickly using this mouse.  I've not had problems with any other mouse.  While the description says "ultra-slim" it's still too wide for me, and I have adult female hands. text_fidelity_a:
Netgear WiFi Dual Band Gigabit Router (WNDR4500-100NAS) Comp: iMac 27inch 2012, Mountain Lion

Installation: easy as 1, 2, 3. It does not get much easier than the install for this router. Working in minutes. Plug in lan cable from router to modem, power on modem, power on router, wait 1 minute (2.4ghz led is lit) turn on web browser. Web browser auto-opens to a simple, SIMPLE, web layout for the routers settings. DONE.

Speed: Excellent speed. Increased speed from an older lynksys router, web pages are opening with noticable % speed increases (as expected from this router)

Range: 5ghz. Router installed on a 2nd floor of 2flr 3200 sq ft home. Installed in 2nd flr bedroom at front of house, ONTOP of computer/work desk. Not ideal placement for the house, but has to be there for now. The dead pockets where signal dropped off on both floors before are now FULL signal. Places like the kitchen and other bedrooms receive FULL signal where solid walls and other electronics are placed. Areas that got marginal or no signal are now are now solid.

Other Equipment: 2 iPhones, 1 macbook, 1 Airport Express (client mode) - full signal strength and speed. Whereas the iPhones would drop in and out of 3G/wifi - they are now solid wifi in all areas of home. Macbook is flying with full strength. Airport Express has not dropped out, at all, like it used to, and seems to be 100% functional.

Conclusion: Cant say enough good things. Price is right, performance is excellent, and range, subjectively, has increased substantially to cover a 3200 sq ft home with the router on the 2nd floor. The ease of installation is fantastic. The pre-set router Network ID & Passwords make this router secure from opening the box and setting up (and easy to change) for those that are looking for security but might not have the know-how or are scared of 'messing up' the newtork.

Great product.
text_fidelity_b: Netgear WiFi Dual Band Gigabit Router (WNDR4500-100NAS)

text_fidelity_a:
KINESIS Freestyle2 USB Keyboard for Mac (9" Standard Separation), Black Overall this keyboard is great. The keys feel nice and they're quiet but not too quiet or soft or squishy. Enjoy typing on this keyboard, pushing the keys seems to take minimal effort and overall it's great.

The best part about the keyboard is that it separates and having the ability to give it a little separation is great. I miss it when I don't have it and it helps avoid torquing the wrists when you are typing. I also love the feel of the keys.

Now before my minor complaints understand two things: (1) I really like this keyboard and despite what I would consider minor defects, I would definitely buy another one. (2) please excuse the fact that I like my keyboards to be consistent and while Apple may not make the *best* keyboards I do use a laptop and I am used to their keyboard layout and feel.

The biggest thing that annoyed me when I purchased this keyboard was the positioning of the ⌘ (command) key. It seems to be shifted over a bit from what I'm used to. Normally I would hit ⌘ with my thumb but it's a little touch to do that on this one given the position of it. It's just something I'm having to get used to.

One minor downside to the keyboard is that the function key doesn't work the same way as the default apple keyboard, rather, the `fn` key is a toggle. I prefer for fn to work as a modifier because that is what I am used to on my laptop keyboard.

Another minor problem is the styling on the caps lock key. Like many people, I remap my caps lock to ctrl and and thus want caps lock to be a normal button. However, on this keyboard the caps lock key is missing the right part of the key so that you don't accidentally hit it when typing the `a` key.

Finally, the escape key and '`' (back tick) keys are in weird positions. The escape key is not as bad as the backtick. There is just something about the distance that I must go that is different from what I'm used to and I have been consistently hitting the `1` key instead. Life goes on.
text_fidelity_b: KINESIS Freestyle2 USB Keyboard for Mac (9" Standard Separation), Black

text_fidelity_a:
Dell Inspiron Gaming PC Desktop AMD Ryzen 7 2700 Processor, 16GB DRAM, 1TB HDD, AMD Radeon RX 580 4GB GDDR5 Graphics Card, Windows 10 64-bit, Blue LED, Model Number: i5676-A696Blu I benchmarked using 3DMark, Time spy. From the results you can see it falls about where you would expect for its hardware and pricepoint. You are going to do better than an entry level gaming laptop, but you aren't going to be blowing anyone out of the water. But... this comp isn't really made for high performance.

It did handle both Minecraft and Ark. If you have kids you may have run into issues with Minecraft being RAM greedy, which is why you want at least 8GB and this has 16GB. So it will handle it with most mods pretty well.

Ark is terrible on computers. Even high end gaming rigs can struggle with it. It is one of the reasons I used it for testing. It is so poorly optimized that it will crash your PC and chuckle at your demise. This computer handled it well on medium settings, which isn't too bad. I wouldn't run epic settings on anything short of a NASA computer, and even still I'd be worried it would crash the space station or accidentally launch missiles.

Bottomline; this computer will make most games playable, they will not be "epic". It's a decent entry level gaming computer. I am not going to tell you to build your own if you want to save money and get a better set up for the same amount. Honestly, if you were of the mindset to do that you would not be considering $700 Dell computers. I have built my own computer, I have also wanted to throw it on the lawn and light it on fire, because when something goes wrong I have no one to blame but myself, and no one to fix it either. So... ignore the "build it yourself" shamers. You do you. If you want to buy an entry level gaming computer go for it. I would strongly recommend saving up the additional $250 to get the upgraded version of this computer though. For not much more, you get a whole heck of a lot more computer. Better processor, better graphic card, way better storage, and an SSD to run your operating system.

I knocked a star for the price and because the driver update software they have on there is a joke. I had to go manually update drivers myself. If that's not your deal I recommend adding a 3rd party driver updater, do not rely on Dells. If you are feeling brave you can buy a more powerful gaming computer for $700, you will just have to do a bit more research that they are a legitimate company.
text_fidelity_b: Dell Inspiron Gaming PC Desktop AMD Ryzen 7 2700 Processor, 16GB DRAM, 1TB HDD, AMD Radeon RX 580 4GB GDDR5 Graphics Card, Windows 10 64-bit, Blue LED, Model Number: i5676-A696Blu
